#44 Jeon (轉)  (647 January)
Arc: The Chunchu Era · place: surabol · tone: political thriller — countdown
Logline: The sixth night’s tea turns to insult, the cavern throws Bidam out, a white horse burns for a falling star, and Yushin’s father’s stone goes warm.
=================================================================
[0] ══ DAY: DAY 6 ══
[1] ¶ Night rain. Five days of grain behind the palace gate. Bidam’s officers want a dawn assault. Bidam wants the score finished properly. He wants Yushin to come out again.
[2] ¶ **Sixth night.** Yushin does not come to the pavilion. Bidam sends tea anyway — two cups poured, one left steaming.
[3] Bidam: …He is not coming today. / Very well. Courtesy held until the sixth night.
[4] ▼ FLASHBACK 610 The headband
    [4.0] ¶ The Hwarang hall, the new boy’s first day. Two seniors lean across his desk.
    [4.1] Senior Hwarang: So he isn’t even a real True Bone!
    [4.2] Bidam: Hey, enough! / What did any of you do to earn True Bone? / You were merely born into it.
    [4.3] ¶ He punches the nearer one before the other can answer, then the second for good measure. Then he wipes his knuckles on his own black headband.
    [4.4] Kim Yushin: Thank you.
    [4.5] Bidam: What is there to thank? / Take this headband. Keep it, and no one will trouble you.
[4] ▲ end flashback
[5] ¶ Near midnight Yushin comes to the pavilion after all. He does not touch the cup.
[6] Bidam: **You Gaya wretch…!** / You dare call yourself the sacred country’s saviour….
[7] Kim Yushin: Lord Bidam. / Fifteen years past, in the Harmony Council — who was it that stood up for Princess Dukman?
[8] Bidam: ……
[9] Kim Yushin: That young Hwarang said he would choose the cleverest of the three. / Where did that man go, Lord Bidam?
[10] Bidam: …That man lived back when the sacred country was still a country.
[11] Kim Yushin: But it is not I who raised a banner against the sacred country…!
[12] ══ DAY: DAY 7 ══
[13] ¶ Seven days in, nobody pours. Four days of grain. Last night’s two cups are still on the pavilion table, and one of them was never touched.
[14] ── SCENE: Not a Kim ──
[15] ¶ **Bidam** finds the cavern the way a man finds a rumor. Sword on the lip. Beads in the fist. The navy coat comes off because he has heard Yushin wash here, and a man who wants what Yushin has will copy the wash if he cannot copy the name.
[16] ¶ He walks into the steam with nothing on but water and one hundred and eight beads.
[17] ¶ The three sisters are already on the far rock. Narim looks at him the way an eldest looks at a door that opened wrong.
[18] ¶ The spring does not hide much. Heat hits him low. He recites. The beads do not help.
[19] (monologue) Bidam: I came to wash. The sutra does not cover this. I am standing in a door I cannot close.
[20] ¶ The beads stop mid-count. He stares. The waterline drops.
[21] Golhwa: Wrong door. He brought iron. And that.
[22] Narim: He is not a Kim. The steam already knows.
[23] Hyullé: …The mouth. Before the water takes the blade.
[24] ¶ They do not stay women.
[25] ¶ Golhwa goes first — fire unfolding into a tiger the size of the rock, ember pelt, steam off the fangs. Hyullé’s silk becomes a water-serpent, long as the bowl, cyan scales. Narim’s elder-shape thickens into a moss-bear, leaves in the fur, the hill’s weight on four feet.
[26] ¶ He recoils. The beads jump. The sword is a hard black line he cannot lift in time.
[27] ¶ They kick him toward the light — tiger-shoulder, serpent-coil, bear-shove. Three beasts, one refusal. The night has him again. The lake keeps Kims. It does not keep slogans.
[28] ══ DAY: DAY 8 ══
[29] ¶ On the eighth night a star falls toward **the Moon Palace** — bright enough that both camps look up. Bidam does not invent the omen. He only names it in a useful direction.
[30] ❝QUOTE (Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 41, Biographies — Kim Yushin; Lee Byong-do ed., vol. 2 (Bidam’s rebellion, 647)): I have heard that where a star falls, blood will surely be shed. This is likely an omen that the woman sovereign will be defeated.❞
[31] Bidam: You heard it. / Heaven has already voted against a woman on the throne. / 女主不能善理 — and now the sky writes it in fire.
[32] ── SCENE: The Moon Palace ──
[33] ¶ The rebel shout shakes the ground. Inside the Moon Palace **Queen Sunduk** goes pale. **Yushin** asks for leave to speak — and for a kite, a torch, and enough lies to edit heaven.
[34] Kim Yushin: Your Majesty — do not fear a falling light. / If they can read a star, they can also unread one.
[35] ¶ He flies the kite from the palace dark: a burning scarecrow rising where the star had fallen, so the night sky seems to take its light back.
[36] Kim Yushin: Look up. / Heaven changed its mind — or we changed heaven’s handwriting. / Hwarang, with me.
[37] ── SCENE: The Stables ──
[38] ¶ The kite buys one night. A sky can only be argued with for so long, and by midnight both camps are already arguing about what they saw. While the drums are still asleep, **Yushin** goes down to the palace stables alone and leads out the white horse.
[39] ¶ **Hangyul** has carried him for eighteen years, since the charge at Nangbi Fortress, to every border the queen sent him to and a few he went to without asking. The groom, a boy of fourteen, works out what the rope in the marshal’s other hand is for before anyone says it, and starts to cry with his mouth shut.
[40] ▼ FLASHBACK 612 Hanbyul
    [40.0] ¶ Seventeen, drunk, and asleep in the saddle. His first horse, **Hanbyul**, does what any good horse does with a sleeping rider and takes him where he always goes. He wakes at the courtesan **Cheongwan**’s gate with her lantern already lifted and her face already glad.
    [40.1] Cheongwan: You came? / …They said you swore to your mother you’d never come again.
    [40.2] ¶ He had sworn it. The horse had not. He gets down, draws, and takes Hanbyul’s head off at the gate in one stroke, then walks home past the lantern without looking at it. The song Cheongwan made about that night outlives both of them.
[40] ▲ end flashback
[41] ── SCENE: The Scorched Ground ──
[42] ¶ The star came down past the west wall of the Moon Palace, where the ground is still scorched in a long smear. Yushin walks Hangyul there himself. **Chunchu** is already waiting with two priests, a bronze basin, and a face that has decided not to argue.
[43] King Muyeol: …There are other white horses. Three in the stable. / Does it have to be this one?
[44] Kim Yushin: They know over there. Everyone knows which horse I ride. / Offer someone else’s horse and it isn’t heaven that laughs. It’s Bidam.
[45] ¶ He takes the halter off with his own hands. Hangyul, who has been led to a great many strange places at night, puts his nose into Yushin’s chest and waits for the reason, as he always has.
[46] Kim Yushin: Eighteen years. / If it weren’t for you at Nangbi, I’d have ended there. / …I’m sorry. This time I’m the one who brought you.
[47] King Muyeol: Yushin. / …Want me to do it?
[48] Kim Yushin: No. / He’s mine.
[49] ¶ He does it the way the rite asks and faster than the rite asks, so the horse never quite finishes turning his head. White goes down into the scorched black. The priests begin the prayer, and Yushin, who has never once let another man finish a sentence for him, lets them.
[50] ❝QUOTE (Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 41, Biographies — Kim Yushin; Lee Byong-do ed., vol. 2 (Bidam’s rebellion, 647)): He slaughtered a white horse and offered it at the place where the star had fallen, and prayed: “In the way of Heaven, yang is firm and yin is yielding; in the way of men, the sovereign is honoured and the subject humble. Should this ever be reversed, there is great disorder.”❞
[51] ¶ Across the field, on the Radiance wall, **Bidam** watches the smoke of the offering go up and asks an officer what was burned. When he is told, he puts his beads away for the first time in eight days and goes down to the lines to stand beside his own horse, **Bisamun**, for a while, saying nothing to anybody.
[52] [battle]
[53] ¶ Afterwards the groom leads out a young grey, too green for a marshal, the only horse left in the royal stable that nobody has been afraid of all week.
[54] Kim Yushin: Name?
[55] ¶ The boy shakes his head. He is still crying.
[56] Kim Yushin: Hanseul. / …It’s easy to say. Stop crying and try it.
[57] ¶ It is the last horse he names. He rides **Hanseul** out on the tenth day, and across the Yellow Mountain fields thirteen years later, and never once lets a groom catch him brushing it longer than the others.
[58] ── SCENE: The Stone ──
[59] ¶ Near midnight, at his desk in the palace, Yushin feels something warm against his wrist. He has carried his father’s stone in his sleeve for thirty years. It has never once been warm.
[60] ¶ He sets it on the desk between the lamp and the grain tally. Chunchu came in to say there are three days of rice left and not to tell the kitchen. He looks at the stone the way he looks at a letter in a script he can’t read.
[61] King Muyeol: …It’s a rock. / Why is your rock warm?
[62] Kim Yushin: My father had it from a spring under the hill. It warmed when the hill wanted him. / It hasn’t since he died.
[63] King Muyeol: And you’re going. With a rebel on the wall and three days of rice. To ask a spring something.
[64] Kim Yushin: Bidam says I was never of Silla. / Six nights I let him say it. I want to know— / …whether I am.
[65] King Muyeol: You’re asking a rock.
[66] Kim Yushin: I’m asking him.
[67] ¶ Chunchu doesn’t argue. He has just watched this man kill his own horse for a sky. He pours out the last of the wine, drinks half, and leaves the other half for whoever comes back.
[68] ¶ Yushin puts the stone back in his sleeve. He will go down before light.
[69] ¶ **A warm stone, a spring under a hill, and a father who once got very lost on purpose. Who was Kim Seohyun…?**

=================================================================
#45 Seohyun  (593)  [FLASHBACK EPISODE]
Arc: The Chunchu Era · place: daeya · tone: forbidden romance into cavern legend
Logline: Before there is a Yushin there is a road, and a young man on it who should be looking where he is going.
=================================================================
[0] ¶ Before there is a Yushin there is a road, and a young man on it who should be looking where he is going.
[1] [MAP 593: ]
[2] ¶ Kim Seohyun is the son of Gaya’s last prince. In the capital, that’s the kind of fact people bring up just after he leaves the room. His father rode in the cart that handed the kingdom over, then spent his life proving it had been a bargain. On one road he took an enemy king, four generals and ten thousand heads. The family is True Bone now. The rank opens most doors in the capital. It opens the best ones least.
[3] ¶ He is young and polite and so used to being the Gaya boy in the room that he apologises before anyone has accused him of anything. He sits a horse better than he sits a banquet.
[4] ¶ The best gate on the street belongs to Sukhuljong, the great king’s younger brother. Royal on every side. His daughter Manmyung is standing in it when Seohyun rides past. He looks. The histories, which don’t usually notice such things, record exactly how.
[5] ❝QUOTE (Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 41, Biography of Kim Yushin, part 1): At first, Seohyun saw on the road Manmyung, daughter of Sukhuljong, son of Galmun-wang Ipjong. His heart was glad, and he courted her with his eyes; and without waiting for a go-between, they came together.❞
[6] ── SCENE: The Gate ──
[7] ¶ The first time, he looks and keeps riding and nearly puts his horse into a charcoal cart. The second time he has an errand ready at the far end of the street, which does not exist. By the third the errand has run out, and he is only a man on a horse going the wrong way slowly.
[8] Manmyung’s maid: Agassi. It’s him again. / Same horse. Same— he’s pretending he isn’t looking.
[9] Manmyung: He’s terrible at it. / Don’t look. …No, look. I want to see what he does.
[10] ¶ Then she does something nobody on that street has seen a Sacred Bone daughter do. She steps down off the threshold into the dust.
[11] Manmyung: You’ve ridden past this gate three times today. / Is the road that bad, or are you lost?
[12] Kim Seohyun: I— the horse— / …It’s lost. I’m only on it.
[13] Manmyung: It looked fine the first time. / Nearly ate a charcoal cart. But fine.
[14] Kim Seohyun: That was— the cart was in the wrong— / Kim Seohyun. That’s— I should have said that first. Is it rude? I don’t know the rule for this.
[15] Manmyung: There isn’t one. That’s why it’s fun. / And I know who you are. Everyone on this street knows who you are.
[16] Kim Seohyun: …Ah. / The Gaya one.
[17] Manmyung: The one with the nice horse. / Then let it get lost again tomorrow. Same hour.
[18] Manmyung’s maid: Agassi—!
[19] ── SCENE: Getting Lost ──
[20] ¶ It gets lost every day for a season. The maid starts timing her errands by it. The charcoal man learns to pull over. Nobody sends a matchmaker, because a matchmaker would have to walk into Sukhuljong’s hall and say the word _Gaya_ out loud.
[21] ¶ By the end of summer they have stopped pretending about the horse. He leaves it at the bottom of the lane and walks up, and she talks to him through the side gate with the bar still down, because a gate with the bar down is technically closed.
[22] Manmyung: You’re late. / The horse?
[23] Kim Seohyun: The horse is fine. The horse is better than me. / They kept us at the Ministry. There’s talk of a posting.
[24] Manmyung: Where?
[25] Kim Seohyun: They haven’t said. North, probably. They send Gaya men north. / Somewhere with a lot of Goguryeo and not much—
[26] Manmyung: Not much me.
[27] Kim Seohyun: …I was going to say not much rice.
[28] Manmyung: Liar.
[29] ¶ Then she lifts the bar. Nobody on that street has seen a Sacred Bone daughter lift her own bar, either.
[30] Manmyung: Come in. / Not the front, idiot. The mulberry shed. Nobody goes in there after dark.
[31] Kim Seohyun: Agassi, I— your father— if anyone— / There are rules for this. I don’t know them, but there are—
[32] Manmyung: Then they’ll have something to talk about besides your horse.
[33] ¶ The shed smells of leaves and silkworms. She has his collar open before he has finished apologising for it. He is a careful man, and she is not a careful woman, and somewhere past midnight he stops being careful too.
[34] Kim Seohyun: That was— I should have— a go-between, a proper— / Your father should have been asked first.
[35] Manmyung: Shh. You talk a lot for a man with no shirt on. / Same hour tomorrow. Bring the horse, so it looks like an errand.
[36] ¶ He comes the next night, and the next. A go-between would have taken a season. They do not have a season. Some nights they barely have the walk up from the lane.
[37] ¶ The posting comes in the autumn: governor of **Manno**, a county far up the Goguryeo road, a wooden wall and a granary and a great many hills that change hands. He comes to the side gate with the seal still in his sleeve.
[38] Kim Seohyun: Manno. / It’s— a long way. Ten days if the passes are open. The house is small. I haven’t seen it, but they said small, and the way they said it— / I’m asking badly. I’m asking if you would—
[39] Manmyung: Yes.
[40] Kim Seohyun: —come with— I haven’t finished.
[41] Manmyung: Then finish. It’s still yes.
[42] ¶ The maid tells nobody. The charcoal man tells everybody. Her father knows by the next morning.
[43] ── SCENE: Sukhuljong’s Hall ──
[44] ¶ Sukhuljong takes the news sitting down, the way he takes most things, without looking up from his cup. He is a king’s son and a king’s brother, and he has never once in his life been the one left standing.
[45] Kim Sukhuljong: Muryuk’s boy. / The one whose grandfather carried his country here in a box and set it on the floor in front of my grandfather. / Him?
[46] Manmyung: His father kept his sword, Father. / You keep a gate.
[47] Kim Sukhuljong: A Gaya chair in a Kim hall. / Every guest who came would sit on it just to hear it creak. / Then you can look at the gate from the inside.
[48] Manmyung: You can’t keep me in a room forever.
[49] Kim Sukhuljong: I don’t need forever. / I need until he leaves for Manno.
[50] Manmyung: It was me, you know. Not him. He’d still be apologising to the horse. / I lifted the bar. Every night.
[51] Kim Sukhuljong: Take her to the back house.
[52] ¶ He shuts her in a house apart at the back of the compound and sets men on the door. Surabol has a word for what the two of them did, and it is not a polite one, and for a few weeks it is the only thing the city talks about.
[53] ── SCENE: The House Apart ──
[54] ¶ The guards are two cousins off one of Sukhuljong’s farms, chosen because they cannot be bribed and cannot read, and by the fourth night they have run out of things to say to each other.
[55] First guard: You think he’ll come?
[56] Second guard: The Gaya one? He says sorry to his own horse. / He’s not coming over a wall.
[57] First guard: I heard he leaves for the north day after tomorrow. First light.
[58] Second guard: Good. Then we go home.
[59] ¶ Inside, Manmyung has stopped eating to make a point and started again because the point was only hurting her. She has counted the boards in the ceiling. At the foot of the back wall, where the drain runs out, there is a gap, and she has been looking at it for three days the way her father looks at furniture.
[60] ¶ On the last night it storms. Lightning comes down on the door itself, and the guards do what men do when the sky picks out the house they are guarding, which is run. In the noise Manmyung goes out through a gap in the wall so low that she has to crawl, in her good silk, in the mud.
[61] Second guard: Heaven— it hit the door, it hit the DOOR—
[62] First guard: Leave it! It’s burning, leave the door, leave it—
[63] ¶ He is at the bottom of the lane with two horses, because he has been there every one of the four nights, in case. He sees a shape come out of the drain on its elbows, stand up and walk toward him through the rain like a woman going to market.
[64] Manmyung: Don’t— don’t look at the dress. / Is the horse lost tonight?
[65] Kim Seohyun: You— the lightning— are you hurt? Your hands—
[66] Manmyung: My hands are fine. Answer the question.
[67] Kim Seohyun: …No. / Tonight it knows exactly where it’s going.
[68] ¶ She kisses him before he can get her on the horse. Hard, in the rain, with drain-mud on her chin and both hands in his hair. The horses wait like men who have seen this before.
[69] Manmyung: …There. Now we can go.
[70] ¶ They ride north in the rain. Behind them, two cousins are trying to explain a door to Sukhuljong.
[71] ── SCENE: Manno ──
[72] ¶ Manno is a wooden wall, a granary, a county office with a leaking roof, and hills that have changed hands more often than the clerks can keep up with. She learns the granary. He learns the hills. Neither of them learns to cook, and by the second month the clerk’s wife has taken pity on them.
[73] ¶ The county house has one room with a door that shuts. The clerks learn not to knock before noon.
[74] ¶ He has a dream on a _gyeongjin_ night and tells nobody for three weeks, because a Gaya man who dreams of stars coming down on him does not say so in a county office. Then, on a _sinchuk_ night, she sits up in the dark and shakes him.
[75] Manmyung: Wake up. Wake up, I had— there was a boy. / In gold. Armour, all gold. He came in on a cloud, right into the hall, through the door like he owned the house. He looked at me.
[76] Kim Seohyun: …I had one too. Three weeks ago. / Two stars. A red one and a yellow one. They came down on me. Not on the house. On me.
[77] Manmyung: Three weeks. / Stars fell on you and you didn’t tell me for three weeks.
[78] Kim Seohyun: I thought it might be the soup.
[79] Manmyung: Pfft— the soup— / Come here, you. Come here.
[80] ¶ She is with child by spring. She is still with child the following spring, and the clerk’s wife, who has delivered half the county, stops coming to check and starts coming to stare.
[81] ¶ Word reaches Surabol before the spring rains do. A Sacred Bone daughter, with child, in a county house, and no wedding anyone was invited to. The city has been waiting for exactly this. Three banquets in a row talk about nothing else.
[82] Kim Seohyun: They’re saying things in Surabol. About you. About— there was no wedding, and now—
[83] Manmyung: Let them. They’re only saying what we did. / And we did it very well.
[84] The clerk’s wife: Twenty months, my lady. / I’ve had cows do it faster. / Either that child is something, or somebody counted wrong at the start, and I won’t say which. You’re the governor’s.
[85] Manmyung: Say it. I want to hear you say it.
[86] The clerk’s wife: …The child’s something.
[87] ¶ The boy is born in the county house at Manno. The clerk’s wife turns him over to wash him. She stops with the cloth in her hand.
[88] The clerk’s wife: My lady. His back. / Look— there. There’s seven. Like someone pressed them in with a thumb.
[89] Kim Seohyun: Seven what?
[90] The clerk’s wife: Stars, sir. The Dipper. On a baby. / I’m going to sit down.
[91] Manmyung: Sit, then. Sit. / And his eyes are some grandmother’s, a long way back. Seohyun says there was a boat.
[92] ❝QUOTE (Samguk Yusa (三國遺事) bk. 1, Marvels — Kim Yushin): Lord Yushin was born in the _eulmyo_ year, the seventeenth of King Jinpyeong. He was endowed with the essence of the Seven Luminaries, and so his back bore a pattern of seven stars; and there were many other wonders about him.❞
[93] ¶ Naming him takes longer than carrying him did.
[94] Kim Seohyun: Gyeongjin. / I want to call him for the night I dreamed. That’s where he came from.
[95] Manmyung: You can’t name a child after a day. / Even I know that, and I ran away from all my tutors.
[96] Kim Seohyun: I know. I know. / But _gyeong_, written down, looks like _yu_. And _jin_, said quickly, is nearly _sin_. / And there was a man in the old books. A scholar. Yu Xin. A good man, they say. / So it isn’t a day. It’s a scholar. Nobody can say anything.
[97] Manmyung: You’ve been working on this for months.
[98] Kim Seohyun: …Twenty.
[99] ¶ They bury the afterbirth on the high hill behind the county, the way you do with a child you mean to keep, and the hill keeps the name.
[100] Manmyung: Yushin. / Say it to my father, next time you’re in Surabol. Say it at his gate.
[101] Kim Seohyun: …He won’t open it.
[102] Manmyung: Then say it louder.
[103] ── SCENE: The Name at the Gate ──
[104] ¶ A few weeks after the birth he rides to Surabol and says the name at Sukhuljong’s gate, loudly, to a street that has stopped to listen. The gate does not open. A steward comes out instead.
[105] Sukhuljong’s steward: His lordship is unwell. / He expects to be unwell for some years. He asked me to say it in exactly those words.
[106] Kim Seohyun: Tell him— / Tell him the boy has his mother’s mouth. / He’ll know what that means.
[107] Sukhuljong’s steward: …I’ll tell him, sir. / He won’t like it.
[108] ── SCENE: The Spring ──
[109] ¶ He rides home the long way because he does not want to arrive yet. The road goes over a ridge beyond the city that nobody uses, and by noon he wants water more than he has ever wanted a shrine. When heat breathes out of the hillside he calls it a spring and gets down.
[110] ¶ Under the hill three sisters keep the heat in the stone, the water in the dark and the moss on the roots: **Golhwa**, **Hyullé**, and **Narim**, the eldest, who also keeps the rules. They have gone centuries without a man coming down to them, and the hill has just told them about hooves on the road.
[111] Golhwa: Hooves! Unni. Unni, hooves. Someone stopped.
[112] Narim: Someone always stops. They drink, they piss in the stream, they leave.
[113] Hyullé: …This one’s crying a little.
[114] Golhwa: Crying? Let me see— move your elbow—
[115] Golhwa: Fox. Let’s be a fox. Foxes are fun.
[116] Hyullé: A grandmother. Then he drinks and bows and goes, and nobody… nobody gets hurt.
[117] Narim: Try both. Then I pick.
[118] ¶ They try both. The fox frightens the horse. The grandmother makes him kneel and offer her his waterskin with both hands, which is so polite that Golhwa groans out loud through the rock. Narim picks the last face herself: three young women in white jeogori over moss-green and ember and pale water-blue, sitting on the far rock as if they had always been there.
[119] ¶ He is still calling it a spring when the ground gives under his boot. He comes down through warm dark into a bowl of black water under stone and stands up coughing in a cloud of steam, soaked to the skin, his sword still somehow in his hand.
[120] Kim Seohyun: Who— forgive me— who lives here? / I was looking for water. There was an old woman just now, up there—
[121] Hyullé: …That was me. Sorry.
[122] Narim: You found your water. All of it at once. / Put the sword down, please. You’ll cut the steam.
[123] Golhwa: Hi. I’m Golhwa. That’s unni. That’s Hyullé, she won’t say hello unless you look at her first. / What’s your name? Say it slow.
[124] Kim Seohyun: Kim. Kim Seohyun. / Are you… I mean. People?
[125] ¶ At the surname all three of them go quiet. _Kim_ is the sound their own steam makes coming off the water, and nobody has ever said it to them as a name.
[126] Golhwa: Kim. / Say it again. No, I heard you. It just… sticks.
[127] Narim: Kim. / …Then the house rules apply. Golhwa. Chin.
[128] ¶ Golhwa is across the pool before he can step back, a wet hand under his jaw, turning his face to the light like a horse trader.
[129] Golhwa: Smooth. Shaved this morning? For who— oh. For the gate. Poor thing. / Chin passes, unni.
[130] Narim: Second rule. Nobody stands in this water dressed. / The steam doesn’t talk to cloth.
[131] Kim Seohyun: I— I have a wife. She’s— we have a son, he’s— / I’m sorry. I should have said that first.
[132] Golhwa: We didn’t ask about her.
[133] Hyullé: …You can turn around. We won’t— we won’t look.
[134] Golhwa: Speak for yourself.
[135] ¶ He turns his back, takes off the wet clothes and folds them badly on a rock, because he does not know what else to do with his hands. Hyullé does not look, mostly. Golhwa does not pretend. Narim waits until he is in the water to the chest and then lets out a breath, which nobody remarks on.
[136] Narim: Today we are the mouths the hill uses when it gets tired of being stone. / Ask it one thing, Kim. From the water. Once.
[137] ¶ He thinks of the gate. He thinks of a girl crawling through a hole in a wall in her good silk.
[138] Kim Seohyun: I have a son. A few weeks old. / My wife’s father won’t say his name. I stood at his gate this morning and said it for him, and— / I don’t know what to ask for him. I don’t know what you ask for a boy like that.
[139] ¶ Their eyes go solid, green and cyan and ember, and the cave stops being funny.
[140] The Hill: The child will be the measure two countries cannot share. / They will call him a blade and mean a border. / When they say he was never of them, the blade will still be Kim. / He will cut more than he is given. Don’t ask who bleeds.
[141] ¶ Narim puts a river stone in his hand, ordinary and grey and too warm for the cave.
[142] Narim: Keep it in your sleeve. / When it’s warm, come back. Same road, same water. One question. / When you’re too old to climb, send the boy.
[143] Golhwa: Shaved.
[144] Kim Seohyun: …Can I tell his mother?
[145] Golhwa: Tell her it was a spring. / Everybody says that.
[146] ── SCENE: Home to Manno ──
[147] ¶ He rides north with a stone in his sleeve that will not cool. At Manno, Manmyung is sitting up with the baby in the lamplight, and she asks him where he has been all day, and he tells her he found a spring.
[148] Manmyung: A spring. / …You’re smiling like a man who found three.
[149] Kim Seohyun: …It was a very good spring.
[150] Manmyung: Mm. / Your hair’s wet. It hasn’t rained in a week.
[151] ── SCENE: Fifteen ──
[152] ¶ The boy grows up at the edge of things, in county houses on the northern road. There’s a younger brother, and two little sisters the house calls by baby names. They’ll grow up to cause a great deal of trouble over a skirt. One of them is Munhee.
[153] ¶ At fifteen he is made a hwarang, and the boys who follow him start calling themselves the Dragon-Flower Band. Seohyun hears it from a clerk before he hears it from his son.
[154] ¶ The morning Yushin leaves for Surabol, his father stops him at the gate of the county house to look at his headband.
[155] Kim Seohyun: You’ve got it on crooked.
[156] Kim Yushin: It’s fine, Father.
[157] Kim Seohyun: It’s crooked. Hold still. / In Surabol they’ll look at the headband before they look at you. They’ll look for anything.
[158] Kim Yushin: Because we’re Gaya.
[159] Kim Seohyun: …Because you’re new. / Mostly because you’re new.
[160] ¶ He reties it with both hands, too tight, and then does it a third time. Manmyung watches from the doorway and lets him.
[161] Manmyung: Let him go. He’ll be late for his own band.
[162] Kim Yushin: Mother—
[163] Manmyung: And stop at your grandfather’s gate on the way. / Don’t knock. Just let them see you.
[164] ── SCENE: Daeyang ──
[165] ¶ Seohyun rises the way a Gaya man rises in the capital. One rank at a time, each signed by someone who remembers the box. By the end he is third rank in the kingdom. He governs the march that faces the enemy, from the fortress at Daeya.
[166] ¶ In the evenings he walks the wall at Daeya. Baekje is a line of hills to the west that the sun goes down behind.
[167] A Daeya officer: They say this wall can’t be taken, sir.
[168] Kim Seohyun: They say that about— every wall, I think. I’ve heard it about four. / Just— keep the granary dry. And know whose hands the keys are in. / My wife ran the granary at Manno. She’d tell you the same. She’d tell you better.
[169] ¶ The histories do not record the year he died, only how high he got. He climbs the ridge beyond the city whenever the stone in his sleeve is warm, shaved every time, until the climb is too much for him. Then the stone goes to his son. The boy with seven stars on his back finds the same water on his own and bathes in it for thirty years, and the stone in his sleeve stays cold the whole time, as if the hill were waiting for a better question.
[170] ¶ **Ninth morning, before light. The stone in his son’s sleeve is warm at last. Down Yushin goes, to the water…!**

=================================================================
#46 Gyeol (結)  (647 January)
Arc: The Chunchu Era · place: surabol · tone: political thriller — countdown
Logline: Yushin asks the water who he is. Then the gate opens from the inside, the yard’s two best meet between the camps, and the score finally breaks.
=================================================================
[0] ══ DAY: DAY 9 ══
[1] ¶ The water under the hill has been warm for thirty years. Before light on the ninth day, so is the stone in Yushin’s sleeve.
[2] ── SCENE: The Lake, Again ──
[3] ¶ So Yushin goes to the cavern lake, as if habit could hold a country together.
[4] ¶ Yushin undresses without ceremony. The three are already in the steam — mentors, tormentors, the only room in Silla where no one asks him for a victory.
[5] ¶ Golhwa knows that walk and is already wet for it. She watches him like a problem she means to solve with her body.
[6] Golhwa: You came early. How flattering.
[7] Narim: He came because he is about to kill a friend. / Forest etiquette: say it plain.
[8] Kim Yushin: If you know that, tell me how not to.
[9] Hyullé: You can’t. / …I’m sorry. / Keep the wound that remembers the headband. Lose the one that wants him to thank you for the blade.
[10] Golhwa: Unless you’re saving all your thank-yous for the Queen again. / She is not in the water, Yushin. We are.
[11] ¶ She takes his wrist under the water and does not wait for the Queen’s name to finish. For a few breaths there is only steam, and the walk they already know, and a marshal who cannot keep his arithmetic. Then Narim’s voice cuts the wick.
[12] Kim Yushin: But Her Majesty —
[13] Narim: Enough, fire. / He will go. We knew that when he took the armour off and still kept her name on.
[14] Hyullé: …Go. / Give Sunduk the victory. / Keep a little silence for us.
[15] Narim: So the stone woke you. / One question, Kim. From the water. Once.
[16] ¶ Steam thins. Two shapes wait where the rock shelves into black: the father who taught him that loyalty is soil, and the grandfather who traded a kingdom so a grandson could keep a sword.
[17] Kim Yushin: Father. Grandfather. / In eight days the same mouth has called me the sacred country’s saviour and a Gaya wretch. / Which of the two do I carry out to the tenth morning?
[18] Kim Seohyun: Yushin, my beloved son. / You were the light of my life, and now the nation needs you to be its savior. / I am sorry that I was not of Silla blood… I tried my hardest to forget my Gaya roots, and tried to pretend that I was something I was not. / But you don’t need to do that anymore. / Son, you are the mighty Sword of Silla, and the Last Prince of Gaya. / But you are infinitely more than that…! / You are my son. You are Kim Yushin. / Your mother and I couldn’t be more proud of you…!
[19] Kim Muryuk: Yushin, my beloved grandson. / When I swore allegiance to the Silla crown, it was not for my own sake, but for yours. / I loved you before I knew you. / Yushin, look at me. / I am so, so proud of you…!
[20] Kim Yushin: Father… / Grandfather… / Thank you.
[21] Golhwa: Look at him — he’s crying.
[22] ¶ He comes up out of the water with the stone gone cold again in his fist. He does not need it warm any more.
[23] ── SCENE: The Outer Works ──
[24] ¶ By midday the ninth day has turned into the battle both sides spent eight days pretending they could avoid. Assault and counter-assault in the outer works.
[25] ¶ Yumjong goes down in the outer ditch with a Silla spear under his arm. Bidam reaches him before the rebels finish falling back.
[26] [battle]
[27] Yumjong: Don’t— don’t make that face, Councillor. / They marched. You said they wouldn’t. They marched… / …It was a good word, though. Gaya. They liked shouting it.
[28] Bidam: Yumjong. / …Yumjong.
[29] ¶ The quieter name on the banner goes first. Bidam closes his eyes for him and does not let anyone see his hand.
[30] ¶ By dusk the granary inside the Moon Palace is down to its last sacks, and men who have never prayed are learning the postures. Alchun is asked, for the last useful time, which wall he belongs to.
[31] Alchun: I belong to the country that survives the week. / If that answer is empty — then so is the chair you will offer me afterward.
[32] ¶ He still does not draw. Surabol will remember that sentence for years: the man who caught tigers, filed under Neither.
[33] ── SCENE: The Rampart ──
[34] ¶ That night, on Radiance’s rampart, Bidam speaks — to his officers, to the wall, to whichever chronicler is still awake. They expect a battle plan. They get a confession.
[35] Bidam: You know… we call this country the “sacred country.” But our country isn’t the greatest in the world. / Its kings are not the most wise. Its armies are not the strongest. / Its men are not the most noble. Its women are not the most chaste. / Our natural scenery is beautiful, but there are more beautiful sights elsewhere. / For every good thing our nation has, there are other nations with greater things.
[36] Bidam: However — that is not why we call it the sacred country.
[37] Bidam: We call it the sacred country, because it is ours. / Because our kings rule over our people. Because our armies are composed of our sons. / Because our men get up every day, and try to make the next day better. / Because our women go to sleep every night, knowing that they have raised our next generation with our blood and our seed. / Because our hills and rivers are the ones that we have grown up with as children — where we used to play with our fathers, and where we will play with our sons.
[38] Bidam: That is what I am defending.
[39] Bidam: The crown may call me a traitor, a heretic, an old man who needs to adapt to the times… / …and to all of that, I simply say no. / I don’t need to say any more than that.
[40] Bidam: And one day, our descendants will prove me right. / So come at me, fate! **Bidam is ready to defend what is ours.**
[41] ══ DAY: DAY 10 ══
[42] ¶ Before the gate opens Bidam goes down to the lines and saddles **Bisamun** himself, which a High Councillor does not do. He slips nine beads off the end of his string and knots them to the bridle, under the horse’s jaw.
[43] ?: Sangdaedeung, those are…
[44] Bidam: Master Wongwang’s fifth precept. Be choosy about killing. / Never the animals that work for you. Horse, ox, chicken, dog. / …They burned a white horse over there two nights ago. Even if I lose, somebody should still be holding on to this one.
[45] ¶ Bisamun is named for the guardian king who stands at the north of every temple with a pagoda in his hand. Bidam rubs the horse’s nose once and speaks to it in the voice he keeps for sutras.
[46] Bidam: You’re named for the one who guards the north. / Today just watch the west.
[47] ❝QUOTE (Diamond Sutra (金剛般若波羅蜜經) §32, tr. Kumārajīva · T08n0235, p. 752b · Sanskrit: Vajracchedikā §32 (Conze ed.)) [Bidam]: All conditioned things are like a dream, an illusion, a bubble, a shadow; like dew, and like lightning. So should you see them.❞
[48] ── SCENE: Between the Camps ──
[49] ¶ On the tenth morning the grain is gone, and the palace gate opens from the inside, exactly as Bidam said it would. Out of it comes the Marshal of Silla at a gallop, on a grey horse that had no name the day before yesterday.
[50] ¶ Bidam rides out to meet him and stops halfway. He gets down, slaps Bisamun on the rump and sends him back to the lines. A spear’s length off, Yushin gets down too. They learned this on foot.
[51] ¶ They meet again between the camps — not as High Councillor and marshal, but as the yard’s two best. Dragon pommel against heavenly horse. The first exchanges are almost gentle. That is how Hwarang kill each other.
[52] ¶ The yard drill first. High guard, cut, step, return. Bidam is fifty-three and moves like it, until he doesn’t.
[53] Bidam: You still drop your left shoulder.
[54] Kim Yushin: You still talk.
[55] ¶ Bidam’s third cut is a feint and the fourth isn’t. It opens a line above Yushin’s brow, right where a Hwarang headband sits. Yushin’s hand goes to his forehead, the way a new boy’s does in the hall when the seniors start in on him.
[56] ¶ Yushin steps inside the next cut, too close for either blade. Bidam’s bead string catches on the dragon ring of his hilt. For one breath they are tied together at the wrist.
[57] Bidam: …Let go, Gaya.
[58] Kim Yushin: You let go.
[59] ¶ Neither does. The string does instead.
[60] ¶ Yushin wins the way a man wins when he would rather lose — late, ugly, through a guard he taught Bidam twenty years ago. The heavenly-horse blade drops. Blood finds the mud that used to be a scoreboard.
[61] ¶ Ninety-nine beads go into the mud after the blood, one at a time, like somebody counting.
[62] Bidam: …One hundred and nine. / Finally.
[63] ¶ Bidam smiles with blood in his teeth — the same boy who once offered a headband across a desk.
[64] Bidam: Hwarang Kim Yushin…
[65] ¶ Yushin does not move to finish it, and there is nothing left to finish. For as long as the breath lasts the two of them look at each other the way they used to across the yard, back when the score was even and neither one wanted to go home.
[66] ¶ Kangrim reads his name three times where the body has not yet finished falling — Bidam. Bidam. Bidam. — the ledger catching up to the last word.
[67] Kangrim: High Councillor. / Your list ends here. Walk with me — His Majesty’s kingdom keeps better minutes than Surabol.
[68] Kangrim: One question, then we walk. / Were you a righteous traitor, or an unrighteous king?
[69] Bidam: …My father asked me that at a gate. / Write that I was his son. / Tell the sacred country I loved it badly.
[70] ¶ The body finishes falling after the name does.
[71] ¶ Bisamun comes through the lines without a rider, at a walk, and stops over him. Nine beads swing under its jaw. When a Silla groom reaches for the bridle it lays its ears flat and shows him its teeth, and the groom, who has had a long ten days, steps back.
[72] Kim Yushin: Leave it. / …Let it go. North.
[73] ¶ Nobody asks him why north. The horse stands there until the body is taken, then turns and goes, past the Radiance wall and up the valley road, and afterwards the officers on the rampart cannot agree whether anyone opened the gate for it.
[74] [battle]
[75] ¶ Yushin kneels once, only to untie the black headband from the body. Then he stands, mud still wet, turns to the Hwarang behind him and names a house. Bidam’s own line. The one he carried in his jaw and never once claimed aloud.
[76] Kim Yushin: Erase Bidam’s house. / The Son line, every one of them. / Treason’s blood must be cut.
[77] Alchun: Yushin… / Bidam is dead. He poured tea for ten days, then took the blade. / If you burn his hall — we erase one of the Six Elders with our own hands.
[78] ¶ Yushin leans close — close enough that the officers hear only breath, and Alchun hears the sentence.
[79] Kim Yushin: Blood is inevitable…
[80] ¶ Alchun goes pale. Down the line an officer asks for the order to be repeated. Nobody repeats it. Yushin mounts, and the order stands.
[81] ¶ Somewhere behind the palace wall, the queen is already slipping away.
[82] ── SCENE: The Queen’s Bedside ──
[83] ¶ Rain finds the lattice before the physicians do. It is a small rain. It beads on the marshal’s sleeve and on the queen’s mouth, and neither of them has a hand free for it.
[84] Kim Yushin: Your Majesty.
[85] Queen Sunduk: General.
[86] Kim Yushin: The physicians are in the corridor. / I told them the rain can wait.
[87] Queen Sunduk: Leave them. / It is a small rain. It will not be what takes me.
[88] Kim Yushin: Your Majesty—
[89] Queen Sunduk: The year I took the crown. You remember. / You said you would serve me to the end.
[90] Kim Yushin: “I will serve you to the end.”
[91] Queen Sunduk: Yes. / And here we are.
[92] Kim Yushin: Did I not promise to stay to the last moment.
[93] Queen Sunduk: You did. General.
[94] Queen Sunduk: …Princess. / Say it the old way. / When you lost the count on the yard, I was a princess.
[95] Kim Yushin: Hwarang. That is what I was. / A hwarang who lost one count.
[96] Queen Sunduk: You do not lose counts.
[97] Kim Yushin: I lost one. / Which one, I will not say.
[98] Queen Sunduk: Then stop being a general about it.
[99] Queen Sunduk: Dukman.
[100] Kim Yushin: …Don’t.
[101] Queen Sunduk: Since the vote I have been Majesty. / Say the name I had before the room.
[102] Kim Yushin: Dukman.
[103] Queen Sunduk: Yushin.
[104] Kim Yushin: I am here.
[105] Queen Sunduk: I know. / Stay. / I can do a little rain.
[106] ¶ The rain keeps on, small, on the lattice and on his sleeve. Her hand stays in his until it does not. The escort waits until the marshal’s hands have finished their work.
[107] ¶ Kangrim reads her name three times — Dukman. Dukman. Dukman. — the ledger’s habit before a Sacred Bone line closes.
[108] ❝QUOTE (Samguk Yusa (三國遺事) bk. 1, Wonders 1 — Queen Seondeok knows three things in advance (善德王知幾三事)): The ministers did not know where that was, and asked, “Where?” The queen said, “South of Mount Nang.” On that very month and day the queen did die, and the ministers buried her on the sunny slope of Mount Nang.❞
[109] ¶ That night Yushin remembers the first morning on the yard, and it is not the way he has been telling it.
[110] ▼ FLASHBACK 610 the twist
    [110.0] ¶ The same desk. The same headband held out across it, still wet at the knuckle end.
    [110.1] Kim Yushin: It’s all right. I will overcome it myself. / My name is Kim Yushin! I will be the great general of Silla!! / Oh — and your name, hyung?
    [110.2] Bidam: My name? Bidam. / That kid…. he’ll be someone great.
[110] ▲ end flashback
[111] ── SCENE: The Empty Pavilion ──
[112] ¶ That night Yushin walks out alone to the pavilion between the old camp lines. The low table is still there, and on it the cup he never touched. He lays the black headband beside it and sits down across from no one.
[113] ▼ FLASHBACK 647 The sixth night · 여섯째 밤
    [113.0] Bidam: **You Gaya wretch…!**
[113] ▲ end flashback
[114] ¶ **The one hand that said no is gone. Now the crown has to fit Seungman, and it was made for someone else…!**

=================================================================
#47 Queen Jinduk  (647 February)
Arc: The Chunchu Era · place: surabol · tone: coronation drama
Logline: The crown was made for her cousin and has to be padded at the temples.
=================================================================
[0] ¶ The crown was made for her cousin and has to be padded at the temples. Seungman sits very still while the goldsmith does it, because somebody told her once that Dukman never fidgeted, and she has believed it for forty years.
[1] ¶ Seungman is crowned Queen Jinduk before the blood on the yard dries. The bloodline’s last polite miracle, stamped and filed while the censers are still warm. The succession Bidam died objecting to passes at last. Unanimously.
[2] ❝QUOTE (Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 5, Silla Annals — Queen Jindeok, yr. 1 (647), 2nd month): Taizong* of Tang sent an envoy bearing his tally to confer on the late queen the posthumous rank of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and to invest the new queen as Pillar of State and King of Lelang Commandery.❞
[3] [CARD Queen Jinduk]
[4] ¶ Alchun is not at the coronation. The court writes his absence down as illness. Everyone knows the illness’s name. It lasted ten days.
[5] ¶ The court does not mean to compare. It simply cannot stop. The old Queen read the peony seeds before they were planted. She heard frogs at Jade Gate Pond in midwinter and sent two thousand men to the exact valley where five hundred Baekje soldiers were hiding. She named the day of her own death and was right about it. The new Queen is gentle, and good at a loom, and has never once predicted anything.
[6] The Court Maids: The old Queen would have known it was going to rain. / Shh. / …She would have, though.
[7] ¶ After the rites, the new queen keeps two men behind. One of them has not had time to wash the mud off his boots.
[8] Queen Jinduk: Yushin… preserve the sacred country…
[9] Queen Jinduk: Bidam…
[10] ¶ She does not finish the name. Everyone in Surabol has heard what Bidam called him by the end. Gaya. Never of Silla.
[11] Queen Jinduk: Yushin… surely Bidam’s words are not weighing on you…?
[12] Kim Yushin: No — what could there be to weigh on me. / I am a loyal servant of the sacred country.
[13] ¶ He says it the way he says the oath on the yard, every word where it belongs. His right hand has closed on his sword belt and does not open. She grew up beside Dukman. She notices hands.
[14] Queen Jinduk: Then let go of the belt, General. / Nobody here is going to draw on you.
[15] ¶ He lets go. It takes him a moment to remember how.
[16] Queen Jinduk: Chunchu. / Unni knew about the frogs before the frogs did. I can’t even tell when it’s going to rain.
[17] King Muyeol: Majesty, nobody asks the moon to be the sun. / They love it because it lets them look straight at it.
[18] Queen Jinduk: …You had that ready.
[19] King Muyeol: Since the funeral, Majesty.
[20] ¶ Then the border spoils the moment, the way borders do. A runner comes in still wearing the road. Baekje is over the western line again, three forts at once. The court turns to the new queen the way it used to turn to the old one, waiting for her to already know.
[21] Queen Jinduk: I don’t know. / Unni would have dreamed it last week. I didn’t dream anything. I slept badly, that’s all.
[22] Kim Yushin: Give me the men, Majesty. I’ll go. / I won’t need a dream to find three forts.
[23] King Muyeol: He’ll win them back. He always does. / And next spring they’ll come for three more. And the spring after that. / Majesty, we can hold the door forever. We can’t make it stop knocking.
[24] Queen Jinduk: Then what stops it?
[25] King Muyeol: A bigger door. / One man alive has an army that size. He lost a summer at Ansi, and he hates losing. / Let me go west and ask him.
[26] ¶ The old queen would have decided this with a smile, as if she had read it in the stars the night before. The new one has read nothing. She looks at Yushin’s hand, which is back on the belt. She looks at Chunchu, who has clearly had this ready since the funeral too.
[27] Queen Jinduk: Yushin, take the men. / Chunchu, go west. / …If you’re both wrong, I want to hear it from you. Not from a runner.
[28] ¶ Outside, it starts to rain. Nobody predicted it.
[29] The Court Maids: …It’s raining. / Did anybody know? / Shh.
[30] ¶ Nobody says a word about the old queen. For the maids, that is the coronation.
[31] ¶ At night she sits at a loom, because her hands want work that nobody will compare. Three years from now she will weave an ode to the Tang emperor into a length of silk, and it will do more for Silla than any prophecy her cousin made. Nobody at court thinks to compare that.
[32] ¶ **Silla needs an army. Only one man alive can lend it, and he has never lent anything for free. Chunchu goes west…!**
